sections.title: Clinical Examination & OSCE Performance
content: Candidates MUST maintain composure: OSCE/VIVA is a 'mind game'—treat it as a professional discussion with a senior colleague.
Always perform a systematic examination: Anterior to posterior approach is standard.
Clinical pearls: When performing Hertel exophthalmometry on patients with unilateral proptosis/exotropia, ensure the eye takes fixation correctly.
Be systematic for Oculoplasty: Always assess Bell’s phenomenon, corneal sensation, and lid lag in ptosis cases.
The 'Wait' Factor: You are not required to answer every question to pass; demonstrate clinical reasoning and safe practice.

rows: PHPV, Retinoblastoma, Coats disease, Congenital Cataract
Bleb leak, Over-filtration, Choroidal detachment, Ciliary shutdown
Pupillary block, Suprachoroidal hemorrhage, Malignant glaucoma (aqueous misdirection)
IIH, Papilledema, Optic Neuritis, Infiltrative/Compressive lesions

sections.title: Oculoplastic & Orbital Emergencies
content: Orbital vs. Preseptal Cellulitis: MUST rule out orbital signs (proptosis, ophthalmoplegia, RAPD).
Facial Nerve Palsy: Assess for CP angle tumor (Schwannoma/Acoustic Neuroma) as a life-threatening cause.
Ruptured Globe: Explore posterior extent of tear; apply first suture at the limbus.
Bell's Phenomenon: Assess strictly before proceeding with aggressive ptosis surgery.

content.explanation: When evaluating Ptosis: P-Position of lid, T-Torsion (intorsion/extorsion), O-Ocular motility, S-Sensory (cornea), I-IOP, S-Systemic associations (Myasthenia: Edrophonium, Acetylcholine receptor antibodies).

sections.title: Posterior Segment: Clinical Protocol
content: Step 1: Media clarity and Disc assessment (look for pallor, cup/disc ratio, peripapillary atrophy).
Step 2: Macular evaluation (dull reflex, fibrous bands, hard exudates, or macular hole).
Step 3: Peripheral retina (look for endolaser marks, tears, or retinal detachment).
Step 4: Complications of Silicone Oil (Glaucoma, Band keratopathy, emulsification).

sections.title: Full Text Archives: OSCE/Clinical Experiences
sections.content: Anterior segment/lids adnexa/oculoplastic: 1) Papilloma photo at lower lid. 2) Post-phaco -2.00D refractive error causes and management. 3) Child with congenital ptosis + Marcus Gunn Jaw winking phenomenon. PCR management in phacoemulsification. Lattice dystrophy photo, RCE management, keratoplasty options. Ruptured globe/IOFB repair protocol. Posterior segment: Thin avascular bleb post-trabeculectomy. NVG with rubeosis iridis. Humphrey 24-2 interpretation/SITA FAST. BRVO complications and management. Macular hole stages and management. RP fundus description and poor vision causes. General medicine/Neuro: Graves ophthalmopathy physiology, IIH investigations/management (refer to neuro), Grand mal seizures management. 3rd Nerve Palsy vs Horner syndrome. Intermittent exotropia management.
